record.context_brief: Dimension of invariant means on LUC(S)
record.original_question: Suppose LUC(S) has a left invariant mean for a semitopological semigroup S. Is the linear span of all left invariant means on LUC(S), equivalently the fixed point set of the adjoint operators of left translations acting on the set of means, necessarily finite dimensional?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.2. Suppose that LUC(S) has a left invariant mean. Does the linear span of the set of left invariant means on LUC(S) (i.e. the fixed point set of the adjoint operators of left translations on the set of means) form a finite dimensional space?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a semitopological semigroup (a semigroup endowed with a topology making multiplication separately continuous). Let $\mathrm{LUC}(S)$ denote the Banach space of bounded left uniformly continuous real-valued functions on $S$, i.e. those $f \in C_b(S)$ for which the map $s \mapsto \ell_s f$ from $S$ into $C_b(S)$ is norm-continuous, where $(\ell_s f)(t) = f(st)$. A mean on $\mathrm{LUC}(S)$ is a positive linear functional $m$ with $m(1)=1$, and $m$ is called left invariant if $m(\ell_s f) = m(f)$ for every $s \in S$ and every $f \in \mathrm{LUC}(S)$. Equivalently, the set of left invariant means is the fixed point set of the adjoints of the left translation operators acting on the (weak*-compact convex) set of means.

Assume that $\mathrm{LUC}(S)$ admits at least one left invariant mean. Question: Must the linear span of the set of all left invariant means on $\mathrm{LUC}(S)$ be finite-dimensional?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem about fixed point properties for semitopological semigroups. Web search returns related results (e.g., for topological semigroups containing exactly n compact left-ideal groups the dimension of left invariant means equals n), but no source providing a complete affirmative or negative answer in the general semitopological setting was found. The status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Invariant means, right ideals and the structure of semitopological semigroups
status_evidence.snippet: Functional analytic properties associated with the existence of an invariant mean on a function space over a semitopological semigroup S.
status_evidence.claim: Related work concerns invariant means and ideal structure but does not settle the finite-dimensionality question in general.

status_evidence.title: Algebraic structure of semigroup (arXiv:1709.09355)
status_evidence.snippet: For topological semigroups containing exactly n compact left-ideal groups, the dimension of left-invariant means equals n.
status_evidence.claim: A partial result yielding finite-dimensionality under specific structural hypotheses, not in full generality.
